title: Fats's serious side: drinking rules and arriving at the studio steady
summary: Fats told the band they could drink as they liked but must be able to play or they had fired themselves; he partied all night yet reached the 8 a.m. sessions with steady hands.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Did Fats have a serious side to him? When he was --

Very. Very. Oh, oh heck yeah, I mean when it came to business, and music, oh man, you -- you never met a man more serious in your life. Never. And, with all our drinking, and bottles he used to buy, and all that business, he'd tell you, said 'now don't get drunk. If you get drunk you fire yourself. You're fired.' He said 'I'm supposed to be the drunken Fats Waller.' He said 'if I can drink whiskey on my job and play, you'll have to.' So if you got drunk and couldn't play, couldn't do your work (smack) you got fired yourself, that's it. He wanted no parts of you.

And if he said 'now I'm not supposed to tell you when to drink, what to drink. That's for you to know, and for you to do. If you don't have the money and I buy you a bottle, I'll sit it there, and I'll use it. You have to take it from there.' And he could drink all night and all day and come to work, come to work, like a clock, and never waver.
Now Buddy, you've got to do the same. And if he

figured you were drunk, and he give you a chorus, he'd say take another one, see? Now see, if you were laboring, and you just get through that first one, there ain't no way in the hell you're going to take it for another one (laughs) and not show it. So you fire yourself.
Well, are you saying that in order to work with Fats you had to be able to drink the way he drank?
No.
Or just don't get drunk.
Drink the way you want to drink, not the way he drank.
I see.

But he drank, and he suggested, he expected you to drink, and didn't think ill of you or mean of you if you did drink. But be able to do your work! That's all he wanted. Just -- just be able to play when your time comes. Do your work.
How did Fats work out on the sleeping? Did he need much sleep? Or could he get along with --

Yeah, he did, he did. He got good -- when he wanted it. I want to say he slept, you didn't see him every night for -- for instance, I've known several times where we're going to record, or we're going to record tomorrow, 8:00 o'clock, be at the studio. He'd stay up all night,

partying all over, oh, Harlem, here, there, downtown, whatever, and get up from wherever he is and walk in the studio. Never late. And Good morning! How are you? Where is -- oh, and his hands are steady, just like that. Where another guy, if he didn't drink, he'd be waving at people he didn't even know.
(Laughter.)
You know what I mean?
Yeah, right.

And he'd say go get me a quart, and he'd come in with a quart of Scotch, and probably send out and get a couple more later on. And he wouldn't eat then. I guess maybe that he'd already eaten before he came in. But whatever he want he'd send his valet out and get it, and get what you wanted for you.

And he just -- stripped down to our waists. I usually, most of the time, because I perspire so doggone much, and then most of the guys would take off their shirt and get down to their undershirts, and we'd go to work. And I mean work!
For a solid what, three or four hours?
Yeah, four hours. That was a session at that time. Four hours, and we ran -- it -- should we run into overtime, we, you know, ran into other things.
